title: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary -- Ch. 13: New Rules on Psychological Incapacity
link: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary (book)
primary_topics: Chapter 13: CJP on the rules on psychological incapacity as a ground to void a marriage under Article 36 of the Family Code
sub_topics: Article 36 — psychological incapacity voids a marriage
Santos v. Court of Appeals — gravity, juridical antecedence, incurability
Republic v. Molina — the guidelines (CJP was ponente)
The movement toward clearer rules for proving psychological incapacity

stances.claim: Psychological incapacity under Article 36 must be grave, juridically antecedent, and incurable, per Santos and the Molina guidelines.

notable_anecdotes: CJP penned Republic v. Molina, which set the guidelines for psychological incapacity.
decision_framework_signals: psychological-incapacity test: grave + antecedent + incurable (Molina guidelines)
one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 13 addresses the rules on psychological incapacity as a ground to void a marriage under Article 36 of the Family Code. CJP traces the doctrine from Santos v. Court of Appeals — requiring gravity, juridical antecedence, and incurability — through Republic v. Molina, which he authored and which set the guiding parameters, and discusses the movement toward clearer rules for proving it.
